title: useRef Simulation (Stable Identity Across Renders)
problemStatement: Implement `createRefContainer(initialValue)` that returns `{ current: initialValue }` whose reference identity remains strictly constant across all calls.
interviewTrap: Thinking updating a ref re-renders the component. If UI needs to visually update on change, you MUST use `useState`.

testCases.name: Returns stable object reference across calls
testCases.testFn: const hook = createRefContainer(0); const r1 = hook(); const r2 = hook(); return r1 === r2;

testCases.name: Allows synchronous mutation of current property
testCases.testFn: const hook = createRefContainer('initial'); const r = hook(); r.current = 42; return hook().current;

testCases.name: Holds non-primitive object or DOM node reference
testCases.testFn: const hook = createRefContainer(null); const r = hook(); r.current = { tagName: 'DIV' }; return hook().current.tagName;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: `useRef(initial)` returns a plain JS object `{ current: initial }` that is guaranteed to be the exact same object reference on every render. Mutating `ref.current = value` is completely synchronous and NEVER triggers a component re-render.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Mutable Container Object Pattern.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Mutable Container Object Pattern maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal
